Definition: Maasejah, the name of sixteen Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Maaseiah is a name worn by many men, and Scripture names them by their work. One was a porter among the brethren of the second degree when the ark was brought to Jerusalem, another was a priest among the sons of Jeshua who had taken foreign wives, and another stood beside Ezra on the pulpit of wood when he read the law to the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the many Maaseiahs show that God calls ordinary men to stand beside His word, whether they carry the ark, confess a sin, or hold up the reader.
